name: Contour Curvature Prediction Error and Approach-Avoidance
prior_calibration: VF-II Doc 64 (Feb 17, 2026) — CCI metric established, partial calibration

mechanism_chain.description: Building edges are extracted by V1 orientation-selective neurons. Angular vertices (high CCI) generate stronger mismatch signals than smooth curves (low CCI) because the visual generative model's contour prediction — which smoothly interpolates edge trajectories — is violated at vertices. P1 component at ~84ms (Leder et al., 2011): earliest EEG marker of contour PE.

data.finding: Curved objects preferred over angular objects; angular contours produce greater amygdala activation
data.effect: Significant preference for curved over angular; amygdala activity higher for angular

data.finding: ERP P1 component at ~84ms marks earliest contour PE detection
data.paradigm: EEG during viewing of curved vs. angular stimuli
data.effect: P1 difference at 84ms for angular vs. curved contours

data.finding: Beauty ratings and approach decisions for curved vs. angular rooms: d ≈ 0.45 (beauty), d ≈ 0.35 (approach)
data.effect: d = 0.45 beauty advantage for curved rooms

justification.backing: Contour PE operates through the fastest visual pathway: angular vertices violate the contour prediction (smooth interpolation) at the earliest cortical processing stage (84ms). The subcortical route to amygdala (Bar & Neta) provides the approach-avoidance valence. Vartanian's VR studies confirm the architectural translation with medium effect sizes.
justification.qualifier: MECHANISM warrant at 0.70 reflects strong neural evidence from both ERP and fMRI. The CCI metric (Contour Curvature Index) provides a quantitative measure. The effect is strongest for simple contours viewed in isolation; complex architectural facades with both curved and angular elements produce mixed signals.
justification.rebuttal: The claim would fail if: (a) the angular-threat association is entirely cultural (sharp = dangerous weapons) rather than perceptual, making it culturally specific; (b) at the scale of architectural facades, individual contour curvature is below perceptual resolution and the effect operates only at feature scale (<1m), not facade scale.

mechanism_chain.description: Contour PE projects to amygdala via subcortical route (superior colliculus → pulvinar → amygdala). Angular contours produce measurable amygdala activation increase; curved contours show reduced activation. Approach-avoidance signal detectable in ERP at ~130ms. Bar & Neta (2006, 2007).

data.finding: Angular contours activate amygdala via subcortical route (superior colliculus → pulvinar → amygdala)
data.paradigm: fMRI with curved vs. angular stimuli
data.effect: Greater amygdala BOLD for angular contours

data.finding: Approach-avoidance ERP signal detectable at ~130ms, dissociable from P1 contour detection at 84ms

justification.backing: The contour PE → amygdala pathway operates through the subcortical route, bypassing cortical object recognition. This explains why the approach-avoidance signal (130ms) precedes conscious recognition yet strongly influences spatial behavior. The amygdala activation is proportional to contour angularity (CCI).
justification.qualifier: Confidence 0.70 reflects convergent fMRI and ERP evidence. The subcortical pathway is fast but coarse — it processes global contour angularity, not fine edge detail. This means the effect applies to prominent architectural contours (rooflines, major structural edges) more than to surface detail.
justification.rebuttal: The claim would fail if: (a) the amygdala activation for angular contours reflects general novelty/salience rather than threat-specific processing; (b) at architectural scales, the approach-avoidance signal from individual contours is overridden by semantic evaluation of the whole building.

mechanism_chain.description: From ~300ms, semantic/contextual knowledge modulates the initial contour PE valence via OFC. Architectural training can REINTERPRET angular PE as intellectually engaging. This modulation is at the EVALUATIVE level, not the perceptual level — the 84ms P1 signal does not habituate with expertise. Knowledge-meaning modifier can reduce effective contour PE penalty by up to 60% for experts in rich conceptual contexts.

data.finding: Knowledge-meaning modulation from ~300ms can override initial contour PE valence via OFC mediation
data.effect: Expert appreciation can reduce CCI penalty by up to 60%

data.finding: Architectural training shifts preference toward angular forms relative to naive observers
data.effect: Significant expertise × curvature interaction in preference ratings

justification.backing: From ~300ms, OFC-mediated semantic knowledge can reinterpret angular contour PE as intellectually engaging rather than threatening. This expertise modulation explains why architects appreciate angular modernism that naive observers find aversive. Critically, the 84ms P1 signal does NOT habituate — the perceptual PE is constant across expertise. Only the evaluative interpretation changes.
justification.qualifier: Confidence 0.60 reflects strong evidence for expertise modulation but uncertainty about the 60% penalty reduction estimate, which is derived from preference shift magnitudes rather than direct neural measurement. The modulation requires rich conceptual context — an angular building presented without contextual information receives less knowledge-meaning benefit.
justification.rebuttal: The claim would fail if: (a) expertise-related preference for angular architecture reflects cognitive dissonance (architects invested in angular design defend it) rather than genuine evaluative re-interpretation; (b) the knowledge-meaning pathway modulates approach behavior but not the underlying threat PE, meaning experts still experience physiological stress from angular architecture that they cognitively override.

exposure_duration.interpretation: 40% of initial d ≈ 0.45 gap persists permanently (perceptual component); 60% decays over ~2–4 weeks. At 2 weeks: d ≈ 0.28; at 4 weeks: d ≈ 0.22.

expertise_familiarity.notes: Perceptual PE cannot be eliminated — only the evaluative consequence. Even architects generate full 84ms P1 PE at high-CCI vertices.

spatial_enclosure_ratio.design_implication: In unavoidable corridors (confining R_h), curved contours compensate for enclosure PE.

cognitive_load.notes: Knowledge-meaning override weakens; CCI tolerance narrows.

interaction_templates.nature: VF1 is the contour-geometry channel of T2. CCI contributes to overall visual complexity PE.
VF1 and VF3 interact additively (Vartanian 2019). Angular + Confining is the worst architectural combination (d ≈ −0.45).
At extreme CCI (>1.80) in memorial/sacred contexts, VF1's high PE contributes to AX3 threshold activation.

key_references: Bar, M., & Neta, M. (2006). Humans prefer curved visual objects. Psychological Science, 17(8), 645–648. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-9280.2006.01759.x
Vartanian, O., et al. (2013). Impact of contour on aesthetic judgments and approach-avoidance decisions in architecture. PNAS, 110(Suppl. 2), 10446–10453. https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1301227110
Vartanian, O., et al. (2019). Preference for curvilinear architecture. Psychology of Aesthetics, Creativity, and the Arts, 13(4), 399–409. https://doi.org/10.1037/aca0000181
Carbon, C.-C. (2010). The cycle of preference. Acta Psychologica, 134(2), 233–244. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.actpsy.2010.02.004

  Architectural experience generates prediction errors across a
  hierarchy of timescales spanning seven orders of magnitude. This
  hierarchy is not merely a catalogue — it reveals that architectural

  different temporal scales, just as musical experience is
  constituted by integration across beat, phrase, section, and
  movement timescales. The temporal hierarchy systematizes what
  previous templates address within their individual domains.

  T-1: MILLISECONDS (50–500ms) — Perceptual PE.
  Contour detection and curvature PE (VF1, ~150ms), luminance
  contrast PE (L1), rapid material evaluation (T9, ~150ms implicit
  evaluation), acoustic onset PE (AX1, brainstem timing).
  These are the fastest architectural PEs — preconscious, automatic,
  and operating on every visual fixation and auditory sample.
  
  T-2: SECONDS (1–30s) — Motor and Navigational PE.
  Motor prediction during movement (TP1, step-by-step), postural
  adjustment (TP1), spatial transition at thresholds (TP2, SC3),
  isovist update as occupant moves (SC2), visual rhythm from
  column/window spacing at walking pace (VF2). This is the
  timescale of active movement through architecture — each step,
  each turn, each threshold crossing.

  The architectural promenade (SC3), the sequence of spatial
  revelations, the emotional trajectory of moving through a
  building. ITPRA cycles at decision points (M5). Navigational
  PE at choice points (SC1). Climactic multi-modal convergence
  (M16, AX3). Subjective time expansion from PE density
  (Wittmann). This is the timescale of a building visit as a
  composed experience.
  
  T-4: HOURS (1–12 hrs) — Occupancy and Adaptation PE.
  Dynamic light changes through the day (L5), thermal drift and
  adaptive comfort adjustment (MAT2), attention fatigue and
  restoration (T25, ART), social encounter patterns (SC4).
  This is the timescale of a workday, a museum visit, or a
  day at home — where initial PE events habituate and the
  building becomes background until conditions change.

  Circadian light architecture (L2, ipRGC → SCN pathway),
  seasonal thermal adaptation (MAT2, de Dear adaptive model),
  cognitive map formation and updating (T3, SC1). Habituation
  of initially novel features; revelation of previously
  unnoticed details. The building shifts from novel to familiar,
  from foreground to background.

cross_template_interactions.IC2_body_budget: High-CCI environments in high-cognitive-load contexts impose sustained contour PE processing cost on a depleted body budget. When cognitive resources to implement the knowledge-meaning override are unavailable, the raw contour PE penalty is paid in full — an IC2 cost imposed on a population that cannot afford it (e.g., fatigued hospital patients).
cross_template_interactions.AX4_perceived_control: No strong direct interaction. If occupants can choose orientation to minimize angular contour exposure, AX4 is weakly engaged.
